title: Take a Walk
coreMove: When thought knots itself, protect a plain walk: feet, breath, and changing sights can carry agitation until the mind has room to see without force.

exampleSpecs.stakes: a public talk can become stiff desk labor instead of living thought
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The same lecture draft changes after a quiet walk, without a labeled diptych.

exampleSpecs.audience: clinicians testing whether movement changes thought quality
exampleSpecs.stakes: better thinking may be blamed on talent while the simple condition is missed
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A current note check reveals that walking changed the draft's quality.

exampleSpecs.audience: students and writers stuck in forced thought
exampleSpecs.stakes: pressure to produce can make the sentence worse
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: private reasoning includes false starts before landing on the walk

exampleSpecs.audience: people trying to force insight from the same stuck position
exampleSpecs.stakes: movement may be reduced to productivity if the person never lets the knot loosen
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The protagonist notices that the walk is not a productivity hack but a change in relation to the problem.

exampleSpecs.stakes: a fast reply may damage trust while a missed review may cost coordination
students may meet philosophy as desk-only abstraction
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: two named people discover the lesson through exchange
